adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that template literals always produce strings, so `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` will always be truthy (even if it's 'undefined: undefined'). This means the fallback `t('unable_to_add_guests')` in `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` will never be used. When err.data?.code is undefined, users will see 'undefined:' prefix in error messages, which is a poor user experience and a real bug.
